response: Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) in children with malignancy is a serious condition. Research suggests that certain factors, such as peak inspiratory pressure, PEEP (positive end-expiratory pressure), and ventilation index values, can help distinguish between survivors and non-survivors by day 3. This information may assist in the early application of supportive nonconventional therapies in children with malignancy and ARDS, potentially improving their outcomes. By identifying these predictors, healthcare providers can take a more proactive approach to managing ARDS in children with cancer and provide more targeted and effective care.
